name: Screw Dislocation
desc: A crystal face growing on its screw dislocations: because a screw turns the surface into a helicoid its step can never grow out, so it winds up into a spiral that pumps terraces outward forever, co-rotating cores braiding into double spirals while opposed pairs close into nested loops, and drifting supersaturation makes the terraces meander and bunch into macrosteps; rendered as Nomarski differential-interference relief, climbing interference orders, luminous risers in dark field, or a blueprint of the step contours.

energy.doc: relief contrast plus how hard the supersaturation bumps meander and bunch the steps

scale.doc: magnification into the crystal face - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: growth rate - how fast the spirals wind out terraces (0.2 still winds)

density.doc: number of screw dislocations on the face (1 to 6) - lone spiral vs a braided nest

terrace.doc: terrace width - a tight dense whorl vs a few broad sweeping steps

hue.doc: hue of the face; dislocation cores take its complement

x.doc: pan across the face when magnified

y.doc: pan down the face when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: Nomarski relief with no outlines at all / climbing two-beam interference orders / luminous step risers on black / blueprint of step contours

seed.doc: deterministic dislocation placement and Burgers signs
